content.page_title: Revascularization and Valvular Heart Disease Recommendations

recommendations.text: CABG should be considered as the first-choice revascularization strategy, in patients suitable for surgery, especially if they have diabetes and for those with multivessel disease.

Coronary revascularization should be considered to relieve persistent symptoms of angina (or an angina-equivalent) in patients with HFrEF, CCS, and coronary anatomy suitable for revascularization, despite OMT including anti‑anginal drugs.
In LVAD candidates needing coronary revascularization, CABG should be avoided, if possible.

Coronary revascularization may be considered to improve outcomes in patients with HFrEF, CCS, and coronary anatomy suitable for revascularization, after careful evaluation of the individual risk–benefit ratio, including coronary anatomy (e.g., proximal stenosis >90% of large vessels, stenosis of left main or proximal LAD), comorbidities, life expectancy, and patient's perspectives.
PCI may be considered as an alternative to CABG, based on Heart Team evaluation, considering coronary anatomy, comorbidities, and surgical risk.

abbreviations.HFrEF: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

12.3.1.title: Aortic stenosis
12.3.1.summary: Aortic stenosis may cause or worsen heart failure by increasing left ventricular (LV) afterload and causing LV hypertrophy and remodelling. When heart failure symptoms occur in patients with severe aortic stenosis, prognosis is poor. Medical therapy alone does not improve outcomes for severe aortic stenosis; guideline-directed heart failure medical treatment should be given to symptomatic patients, but use of vasodilators requires caution to avoid hypotension. Potential symptomatic improvement with medical therapy should not delay definitive intervention.
